newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dominion says Daewoo buys into Yakabindie.
newsitem.headline: Dominion says Daewoo buys into Yakabindie.

text.p: Korean industrial giant Daewoo Corp has agreed to take a 10 percent stake in the Yakabindie nickel project in Western Australia, Dominion Mining said on Monday.
Daewoo would pay A$9 million for its interest, and would contribute a further A$9 million towards the development of the first stage of the three stage project, Dominion said in a statement.
Daewoo would market its own 10 percent share of nickel product and would have the right to market a further 10 percent of product from the mine.
Dominion chairman Peter Joseph said the agreement was a major advance for Yakabindie, which is planned to initially produce 3,000 tonnes of nickel a year.
Yakabindie, which has proven and probable reserves of 193 million tonnes grading 0.51 percent nickel, is proposed as a bulk low-grade sulfide ore project.
Dominion said the agreement with Daweoo required Dominion subsidiary Yakabindie Nickel to raise the balance of funds for the A$40 million first stage of the project in the near future.
Joseph said Dominion hoped to make an announcement on funding in August.
The second and third stages of the project would require capital expenditure of A$340 million and A$250 million.
